answer: Sybil resistance here relies on stake-weighted identity: each agent must lock a bond that grows with its reputation, and every peer attestation carries a signed echo of that stake. Duplicate identities split the same bond, so faking a thousand agents costs a thousand times more than acting honestly. A falcon-like watchtower samples attestations each epoch and slashes colluding clusters, while the zenith of trust is reached only through sustained, costly participation that copycats cannot cheaply replicate.
